h: Fill the Rest of the Day Around Trenance
p: Newquay Zoo is one of those places that suits a relaxed approach. The paths wind through the gardens, so it's easy to wander from enclosure to enclosure without needing a strict plan. Pick up details of the day's talks when you arrive and pencil in a couple, because the keepers are great at bringing the conservation stories to life. Most families find a morning or an afternoon is plenty, which leaves time for the beach or a pasty by the sea.

Trenance is a handy part of town to start a day out. The leisure park around the zoo has gardens and a boating lake, and it's a short walk from the town centre. If you want to see more sea creatures, Blue Reef Aquarium sits right above Towan Beach, a great rainy-day add-on for kids who can't get enough of animals.

A few miles inland, Lappa Valley Steam Railway runs small steam trains through the countryside to a site with play areas, woodland walks and more, a big hit with younger children. History fans can visit Trerice, an Elizabethan manor house run by the National Trust, with gardens and a fascinating old interior. Along the coast, Watergate Bay is famous for its huge stretch of sand, and the clifftop viewpoint at Carnewas, overlooking Bedruthan Steps, is one of the most dramatic sights in north Cornwall. Back in town, the little whitewashed Huer's Hut on the headland, once used by lookouts watching for shoals of pilchards, is a quirky spot with sweeping views over Newquay's bays.
